scope: Independent semantic review of supplied PDF reference corrections. Read-only; only this peer-review artifact written. Source strings and audio must remain baseline.

dhyanaDecisions.text: prodyad divākara samānatanuṁ sahasra sūryoru dīdhitibhir āpta samasta lokaṁ
dhyanaDecisions.reason: PDF bhir āpta parsing is compatible with noisy acoustic virāpta; the matching complete verse makes this a compound description, not a new recited action.
dhyanaDecisions.suggestedMeaning: Of a form like the rising sun, whose great radiance, like that of a thousand suns, reaches or pervades all worlds.

wordAdjustment.āpta: reached or pervaded; in āpta-samasta-loka, describes the worlds reached by his rays

dhyanaDecisions.reason: jñānābhayāṅkitakaram is supported by PDF and acoustic shape; correction repairs only the first hand compound. Retaining jñānādi bhayāntikaram and kapilaś ca preserves the recorded restart and variant. Keep the second joining explicitly unresolved.

ravīndvamita matches ravi + indu + amita and the continuous acoustic ravīndu-mīti; PDF labels its printer repair. Keep that qualification. Do not import the PDF’s imperative interpretation of smaratorugīrbhiḥ in the following line: it qualifies the Hanuman-led recipients who remember/praise him.

Hari + maṇinibham is a defensible resegmentation of acoustic harirmaṇi and PDF reading. dhyāyed dharim reflects external t+h sandhi; word gloss must explicitly identify underlying harim so dharim is not taught as a separate deity/lexeme.

paraśvadhadhanurdharam correctly describes the axe-and-bow bearer; no recorded phrase is omitted. The proposed line-level active 'pervading' and word-level passive 'pervaded' should be phrased without a false certainty about the damaged radiance construction.
dhyanaDecisions.suggestedMeaning: Ember-colored, with radiance extending all around beyond the cosmic sphere, bearing axe and bow, the unique hero.

dhyanaDecisions.reason: agryaśaktim fits PDF's explicit minor correction and phonetic agra/samagra shape; preserve raw source and visible reference qualifier. The koṭi component can be explained as ten million/crore, rather than only vague plural millions.

wordAdjustment.tigmāṁśukoṭyadhikatejasam: whose brilliance exceeds that of a crore (ten million) suns; tigmāṃśu = sun, koṭi = crore, adhika = surpassing, tejas = radiance

dhyanaDecisions.reason: Fine acoustic witness actually gives paripūritāntar bākṣyāṇḍakośam, compatible with supplied PDF antaḥ-bāhyāṇḍakośam and less compatible with baseline brahmāṇḍa. Do not overwrite with familiar parallel text. The parts form a whole inside/outside compound; bāhya should not be taught as an independently asserted new 'outer sphere'.
dhyanaDecisions.suggestedMeaning: His radiance of knowledge fills the cosmic sphere within and without; his appearance is like an emerald.

wordAdjustments.paripūritāntaḥ: filled throughout within; first part of the reference compound paripūrita-antaḥ-bāhya-aṇḍakośam
wordAdjustments.bāhyāṇḍakośaṁ: outside the cosmic sphere, joined with antaḥ 'within' in the preceding token; compound describes the cosmic sphere as filled within and without

dhyanaDecisions.reason: ānato 'smi is supported by acoustic ānatoṣmi and PDF; the avagraha marks elided a rather than new speech. Knowledge/reasoning and fearlessness gestures are deity attributes supported directly by Tantrasara Sanskrit commentary. No practitioner hand gesture may be inferred.

layoutAssessment: Each proposal preserves the existing learning-line identity, source-local replay interval, block boundaries and null stanza breaks. Joining damaged compounds legitimately changes lexical row token count; it should not merge or duplicate learning lines. Recorded restarts remain in their original line. Every afterText whitespace token must still have an ordered word gloss, including attached punctuation if present.
sourceSafeguards: Keep baseline sourceOriginal and sourceRoman byte-for-byte, even when displayed Sanskrit is repaired.
Keep section/block/line order, recorded repetitions, audio paths and all replay times.
Do not append booklet-only Hayagriva/Lakshmi nectar-bathing lines, repeated Gayatri, invocation formulas or alternative Visarjana mantras.
Do not copy a PDF English interpretation when the Sanskrit grammar or actual spoken variant contradicts it.

presenceDecisions.reason: Accept feminine lotus-eyed epithet: independent acoustic netrāṃ plus PDF resolves the erroneous masculine ending. Preserve this distinct Lakshmi two-lotus description; do not replace it with booklet Bhu objects.
Accept feminine lotus-eyed recovery, with audible betel/blue flower and distinct Bhu attributes retained.

Accept tarjana over dara/conch: fine/coarse darjun and PDF tarjana supply a better compatible lexical parse. Both cakrābja occurrences and the actual triśūla word remain; no practitioner gesture is implied.

wordAdjustment.tarjana: admonishing or threatening gesture, an attribute of the deity; no practitioner motion prescribed

presenceDecisions.reason: Accept the supplied-booklet acyutāṅke lap reading: fine acchutāṅgē and coarse acyutāṅge do not support the added gh/r of baseline feet. This is a reference-backed recorded variant relative to the different Tantrasara feet text, not a claim that every edition reads lap. nutinityavacaḥ remains the recorded uncertain compound, rather than importing PDF nutinutya.
Accept gadābhayakaraṃ: both stored acoustic witnesses have gadā onset and PDF specifies mace. Preserve the separate añjali description; do not impose a number of hands or practitioner mudra.

Accept clarified technical Prana-line sense as reference-assisted interpretation. Retain the extra recorded śrī syllable and its unresolved status; do not assert a second goddess invocation or describe an unprinted ritual motion.

Accept sarvavidyā draṣṭṛ repair of acoustic sarvavedyādṛśkṛṣṭ while retaining both Veda-presiding utterances. Nested attribution of the compounds is not fully secure; explicitly qualify the line meaning rather than presenting the proposed plural seers as an exact resolved syntax.
presenceDecisions.suggestedMeaning: [Reference-assisted reading; nested syntax remains provisional:] I bring Vyāsa in feminine form into my presence, indwelling revered Brahmāṇī and Bhāratī, associated with seeing all knowledge and presiding over the Vedas; the Veda-presiding expression is repeated.

presenceDecisions.reason: Accept Jayanti proper-name recovery and Prīti decomposition supported by the supplied reference. Recorded śrīmāyā/kṛti/śānti remain; do not change to PDF hrīṃ Māyā or remove the first list before its restart.
Accept Prīti meaning correction while preserving the repeated Janaki/Satya/Rukmini list and compound word slot.
Accept Gungu and Sinivali reference-assisted name spellings. Preserve recorded Varuni ending and avoid unsupported substitution/equation with Kuhu.
Accept recognizable Jayatirtha proper-name recovery; retain actual kṛtān rather than imposing PDF kartṝn.

Direct review of Aitareya Brahmana3.24 confirms gṛhā vai pratiṣṭhā sūktam as a Vedic identification in its original sequence of stotriya/soul, anurupa/offspring, dhayya/wife and pragatha/cattle. Haug explicitly interprets the hymn as house/firm footing. The booklet’s practical label does not justify erasing the original hymn/homes metaphor. Retain the spoken words and explain both homes/foundation and the hymn relationship.
presenceDecisions.suggestedMeaning: The hymn represents homes, a firm foundation; it should be praised with speech that is most firmly established.

wordAdjustments.gṛhā: homes; Vedic nominative plural, here the image with which the hymn is identified
wordAdjustments.sūktaṁ: the hymn, identified here with homes as a firm foundation; also used as the passage label in the puja booklet

evidence.passage: gṛhā vai pratiṣṭhā sūktam, then tatpratiṣṭhitatamayā vācā śaṃstavyam; Haug house-as-firm-footing interpretation at displayed lines218–234

presenceDecisions.reason: Accept fuller translation of both yad and arghyādibhiḥ occurrences. Do not replace recorded yad-yad restart with PDF adya or erase repeated offering phrase.

Accept visibly marked reference-assisted tvaṃ nominative recovery; an ASR-lost nasal is plausible. The PDF confirms coherent second-person syntax. Keep actual yāgāvasāna rather than alternate pūjāvasāna; audio/source strings unchanged.
Accept Sarasvati+atmaka sandhi repair. Keep actual Navaratri/Ashtami and Vedavyasa formula; no imported Parashurama or new sankalpa.

Accept semantic clarification of singular bhagavān as the Lord in associated Vyasa/Parashurama forms, preserving Sarasvati/Mukhyaprana indwelling phrases and all source tokens. śrī is honorific here, not a separate Lakshmi invocation.

limits: Stored ASR is an acoustic witness, not personal listening certification. Qualified reference repairs and unresolved variants must remain visible. The supplied English/IAST PDF itself marks several printer/grammatical repairs and should not be treated as an infallible edition.

presenceSectionUpdateDecisions.reason: Necessary corresponding lap/praise/power correction; it describes meditation on the deity and adds no practitioner movement. Keep action unchanged.

rejectedOrPreservedDifferences: Keep recorded Bharati echoes, Saraswati ātmavidyāṃ versus booklet ātmasaṃsthām, separate Śrī/Bhū descriptions, original Aitareya Vedic identification rather than replacing it with an exclusive modern passage-label explanation, and actual Visarjana formula. Booklet-only Brahmanaspati dismissal and book-moving action are not authorized additions.
